Instructions for submitting Observer reports 

Introduction 
This document provides the reporting template and instructions for Observers to report 

during the 2023 - 2025 Norwegian Chairship of the Arctic Council. 

The deadline for submission is 1 December 2024. 

 

Role of Observers 
The role and responsibilities of Observers, as well as criteria for admission to the Arctic 

Council, can be found in the “Arctic Council Rules of Procedure” (Annex 2) and the 

“Observer Manual for Subsidiary Bodies.” 

The primary role of Observers is to observe the work of the Arctic Council. Observers 
contribute to the Arctic Council primarily through engagement at the level of Working 
Groups, Task Forces, and/or Expert Groups. Observers are invited to the meetings and 
other activities of the Arctic Council unless the Senior Arctic Officials decide otherwise. 
Observers may also propose projects through an Arctic State or a Permanent Participant. 

Report submission 
Observer reports should include the relevant information described below and in the 
template. 

(a) A description of the Observer’s contributions to the work of the Arctic Council since 
the time of the Observer’s most recent submission, or in the previous two years, with 
special focus on contributions to the subsidiary bodies through project participation 
and support, as well as collaboration with Permanent Participants; 

(b) If applicable, a description of the Observer’s future plans to contribute to the work of 
the Arctic Council, with special focus on contributions to the subsidiary bodies 
through project participation and support, as well as collaboration with Permanent 
Participants; and, 

(c) If applicable, a description of the Observer’s contributions to other aspects of the 
Arctic Council and its goals not covered in the previous sections since the time of the 
Observer’s most recent submission, or in the previous two years. 

 

Observer reports should be submitted electronically to the Arctic Council Secretariat via 

email: acs@arctic-council.org not later than 1 December 2024. Please bear in mind while 

preparing your report that all Observer reports will be published online in the Observer 

section of the Arctic Council online Library (OAR) following the Chairship transition. 

If an Observer fails to submit a report, the Arctic Council will consider this to mean that the 
Observer is no longer interested in maintaining its status as an accredited Observer to 
the Arctic Council.

Observer Report 
Please describe in no more than two pages your State’s or Organization’s contributions to 
the work of the Arctic Council’s Working Groups, Task Forces, and/or Expert Groups since 
the time of your most recent report, or in the previous two years. Please highlight 
contributions to specific projects, such as through proposals, concept development, in- 
kind and financial support, and hosting of meetings. Please detail any collaboration with 
Permanent Participants, such as project proposal endorsement and support. 

1. Promotion of Arctic Challenge for Sustainability II (ArCS II) 

Japan has been promoting the Arctic Challenge for Sustainability Ⅱ (ArCSII) as a national 

flagship arctic research project. Under the four strategic goals such as advanced observation, 

advanced prediction, impact on society, and social implementation with legal and policy responses, 

comprehensive studies have been implemented by utilizing research infrastructure such as 

international collaboration sites, research vessels, satellites data, and Arctic data archive System 

(ADS). 

The implementation of ArCSⅡ will be completed during this fiscal year. Once the results 

have been compiled to a certain extent, ArCSⅡ’s data will be considered for publication through 

online and other methods. 

 

2. Japan’s Contributions to the Work of the AC subsidiary Bodies 

ArCS II has sent Japanese researchers to the AC's subsidiary bodies to provide useful inputs 

from the scientific point of view. See Japan’s contributions to AC's subsidiary bodies as follows: 

- ACAP: 

Dr. Sueyoshi Tetsuo from NIPR and Dr. Sugiyama Shin from Hokkaido University participated in 

the ACAP Working Group (WG) meeting held in September 2024. 

- AMAP: 

Dr. Enomoto Hiroyuki from NIPR, Dr. Kikuchi Takashi and Mr. Kimura Hajime from JAMSTEC 

participated in AMAP meetings (both webinars and observer dialogue). 

-Three members, Dr. Yoshimori Masakazu, Dr. Ukita Jinro from the University of Tokyo and Dr. 

Kobayashi Hideki from JAMSTEC, have been selected as the AMAP Climate Update 2026 Report 

Expert Group. 

-Dr.Kikuchi Takashi and Mr.Kimura Hajime have contributed to the creation of the AMAP Observer 

Reporting 2024. 

- CAFF: 

The Ministry of the Environment (MOE) and Dr. Uchida Masaki from NIPR participated in the 

CAFF board meetings. 

Japan has been holding events especially focusing on Arctic Migratory Bird Initiative (AMBI) 

priority species. Japan’s contributions to AMBI are as follows: 

-From February 2020 to January 2023, Japan held meetings on migratory patterns and the effect of 

climate change with domestic experts to protect Arctic-breeding migratory birds. The results were 

compiled into a report and shared with relevant stakeholders and wetland managers across the 

country and its debriefing session was held online in May 2023. 

-Since 2021, Japan has been hosting meetings with domestic experts to share the information on 

the ecology of Dunlin, which is a priority AMBI species, to review and analyze factors that may 

pose threats, and to exchange views on conservation measures for eliminating such factors.

-Since 2000, Japan has been conducting annual surveys to estimate the population of shorebirds 

including Dunlin and continue color-flagging of the species to identify their survival rate over 

winter. In addition, DNA analysis was conducted from 2021 to 2023. Furthermore, since 2024, 

tracking surveys of Dunlin by attaching satellite devices to captured individuals have been 

conducted to clarify small-scale movement patterns and habitat use during the wintering period. 

-In January 2023, Japan sponsored a waterfowl survey focusing on AMBI priority species in 

coastal wetlands at Thailand, and conducted interviews with the Thai government’s Office Of 

Natural Resources and Environmental Policy and Planning (ONEP), the Ministry of Natural 

Resources and Environment (MNRE) and relevant stakeholders. 

 

-NIPR reported the articles below, which related to CBird project. 

In 2022, NIPR published the article which showed the increasing use of the northern sea route had 

an impact on polar seabirds. 

https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/marine-science/articles/10.3389/fmars.2022.875541/full 

 

-PAME: 

Dr. Otsuka Natsuhiko participated in PAME working group meetings and Shipping Expert Group 

(SEG) meetings. In addition, Japanese researchers contributed to the creation of PAME-MPA 

Framework of the AC and the work for update of “Framework for a Pan-Arctic Network of Marine 

Protected Areas 2015” for the next 10 years in the AC. At this time, Research Director of Strategic 

Goal 4 of ArCSⅡ and researchers, who participated in PD, SPD, PAME, CAFF and SDWG 

discussed the importance of the opinions of indigenous people. 

-SDWG: 

Dr. Ohnishi Fujio from Hokkaido University was originally scheduled to participate in SDWG 

Regular meeting in October 2024 but could not attend the meeting this time due to the schedule. 

-EGBCM: 

Regarding the creation of the National Report for EGBCM of the AC, Dr. Tanimoto Hiroshi from 

the National Institute for Environmental Studies submitted the Japan’s National Report for 

EGBCM, which described the current situation and future projections of black carbon and methane 

in Japan to the Arctic Council Secretariat in August 2024. 

- EPPR: 

Although ArCSⅡ had not sent researchers to EPPR, the Japanese government participated in 

EPPR online meeting in November 2023.

If applicable, please describe in no more than one page your State’s or Organization’s 
future plans for contributing to the work of the Arctic Council’s Working Groups, Task 
Forces, and/or Expert Groups. Please highlight intentions to contribute to specific projects 
and to collaborate with Permanent Participants. 

 

1. Cooperation with Indigenous People 

Japan has been pushing forward, and will continue, its efforts as an observer to contribute to 

the work of the subsidiary bodies of the AC in order to provide useful inputs from a scientific point 

of view. 

Japan also recognizes the importance of cooperation with the Permanent Participants. As an 

example of cooperation with indigenous peoples, the Coastal Environments program of ArCS II 

has conducted surveys of landslides, waste disposal, and living environments around Qaanaaq in 

northwest Greenland, in addition to the joint observations of glaciers and marine ecosystems that 

have been conducted every summer since 2021. 

In Siorapaluk, adjacent to Qaanaaq, a series of large surface landslides occurred in 2016 

and 2017 due to extremely heavy summer rains. Through field investigations, Japan clarified the 

mechanism of the landslide events, then produced and provided a landslide hazard and surface 

deformation map based on synthetic aperture radar (PALSAR-2) data from JAXA's ALOS-2 

satellite. Japan also investigated the contamination levels around the landfill (garbage site) and 

found that the cadmium and lead concentrations in the mussel samples exceeded the criteria set by 

the EU. Japan has already presented these results for a workshop with the people of Qaanaaq and 

discussed these preventive measures. Japan also met with a member of the Greenland Parliament 

elected from Qaanaaq to discuss how to effectively communicate these results to local residents. 

In the near future, Japan will provide the report written in the local language, translated in 

cooperation with the local residents to further raise awareness and disseminate the report to the 

local community. Japan also plans to visit Nuuk, Greenland in November or December 2024 to 

provide a comprehensive report to the Greenland government. 

 

2. The Construction of the Arctic Research Vessel “Mirai II” 

The Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology (JAMSTEC) is progressing 

with the construction of Japan’s first research icebreaker, the Arctic Research Vessel “Mirai II,” 

which is scheduled to enter service in fiscal year 2027. As an international research platform, Japan 

aims to expand observation activities in cooperation with relevant countries. In addition, in order to 

contribute to the development of young scientists engaged in arctic studies, Japan is considering 

the implementation of an international open call for on-board researchers. 

 

3. “The Industry-Academia-Government Collaboration Council about the NSR” 

The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) conducted a survey to 

understand the possibility of future utilization of the NSR by Japanese shipping companies. 

In addition, MLIT is in contact with the Industry-Academia-Government Collaboration 

Council about the NSR to resume the activities of the Council. 

MLIT will continue to enhance Japanese companies’ understanding of the NSR and will 

also make efforts to support their endeavor to utilize the NSR through collaboration with various 

stakeholders.

1. Latest Updates of Japan’s Policy on the Arctic Issues 

Surrounded by the oceans and with the world’s sixth largest maritime areas under its 

jurisdiction, the Headquarters for Ocean Policy of Japan formulated a multi-year “Ocean 

Development Strategy” in April 2024. One of the six key missions of the Strategy is to promote 

international collaboration based on Japan’s Arctic Policy, which was formulated in 2015. In line 

with this policy, Japan reiterated its commitment to steadily promote (1) scientific research, (2) 

exploration of possibilities for sustainable development, and (3) contribution to international rule-

making in the Arctic, in cooperation with the Arctic Council member countries and other 

appropriate possible partners, taking into account the current international situation. Through these 

efforts, Japan will promote understanding towards Japan’s Arctic policy, strengthen cooperation 

with the Arctic Council member countries and other related countries, and make contributions in 

the Arctic. 

 

2. Organizing the Arctic Circle Japan Forum 

The Arctic Circle Japan Forum was organized by the Arctic Circle, the Sasakawa Peace 

Foundation and the Nippon Foundation in Tokyo in March 2023. The Forum was attended by 

approximately 300 participants, including parliamentarians, government officials, researchers, 

business people and nonprofit organizations from roughly 20 participating countries and regions. 

This was the first Arctic Regional Forum held in Japan, and it was highly appreciated by the 

participants. 

From the Japanese government, Ms. Nagaoka Keiko, then Minister of Education, Culture, 

Sports, Science and Technology, and Mr. Nishimura Akihiro, then Minister of the Environment, 

took the podium, and the remarks of Mr. Hayashi Yoshimasa, then Minister of Foreign Affairs, 

were introduced in the closing session. 

Mr. Takewaka Keizo, Ambassador in charge of Arctic Affairs, spoke about Japan’s 

contribution to the Arctic Council, the rule of law, the importance of a free and open Arctic, and 

Japan’s commitment to zero emissions in Asia. 

 

3. Japan’s Other Diplomatic Activities to Promote International Cooperation on the Arctic 

Issues 

 Mr. Takewaka Keizo, Ambassador in charge of Arctic Affairs, participated in the Arctic 

Encounter Symposium in Anchorage in March 2023 and April 2024, and participated in the panel 

discussions on Japan’s investment in the Arctic and diplomacy. He also participated virtually in the 

Warsaw Format Meeting, and explained about Japan’s research activities in the Arctic in June 2024. 

He also participated in the Arctic Frontiers and discussed the Arctic issues in January 2022-2024. 

Dr. Enomoto Hiroyuki of NIPR attended the One Planet-Polar Summit in November 2023 

and the Arctic Circle in October 2024.
